data.narrative:
Copenhagen Atomics is a Series A nuclear energy company that has raised $25M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 11 comparable companies—3 public (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private entities including Fuse Energy, Helion, Valar Atomics, X-Energy, and Oklo—all operating in frontier nuclear technology.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using the $25M total raised as a proxy base value and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A advancement, implies a valuation of $50M. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—Valar Atomics ($6.0B, Series B), Nano Nuclear Energy ($808M, Seed), and Fuse Energy ($200M, Series A)—yields a median valuation of $808M, with a range spanning $200M to $6.0B. The wide peer dispersion reflects early-stage heterogeneity in the nuclear energy subsector.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $42M (low) to $929M (high), with a median of $429M. This 22x spread between low and high estimates reflects material uncertainty inherent in early-stage frontier-tech valuation. Key drivers of variance include stage-progression sensitivity to assumed multipliers and the extreme heterogeneity within the peer set—particularly the $6.0B outlier (Valar Atomics, Series B) versus the $200M floor (Fuse Energy, Series A). Refinement would benefit from narrower stage-matching and clearer visibility into Copenhagen Atomics' technical differentiation relative to peers.
